why: skinScroll is THE place "is this skin animated?" is answered (its own doc comment), and issue #473 moved it from game/customization.ts to presentation/customization.ts. Returning null for every skin freezes flow's texture drift. 1 of 105 across entities.test.ts and preview.test.ts: entities.test.ts's flow-drift case (0.08 repeats/s over 0.5 s of dt) is the kill, which is the proof that the renderer reads the MOVED definition rather than a copy. Stated remainder: preview.ts's second consumer, `controls.setAnimating(skinScroll(skin) !== null)`, is not pinned by preview.test.ts and survives here. RE-MEASURED at 2 by issue #651: entities.test.ts's new 'holds the texture offset under reduced motion' case ends by turning the policy back OFF and asserting the drift RESUMES to 0.04 -- the same 0.08 repeats/s the original case pins, so the same null return kills it. That resume half is the assertion proving the flag is not a one-way latch and is worth the second failure; the reduced half alone passes under this mutation, since a null scroll also moves nothing.
